title: Nonce-lock head-of-line policy (priority lane or abortable escalation) and re-entrancy detection (throw vs deadlock)

options.name: Keep current behaviour: one strict first-come queue per wallet, held for a whole escalation; a nested acquire is not detected
options.risk: An anti-rug exit can wait about 4 minutes behind a snipe that does not land, gives up after 60 s and then runs late at whatever price is left (AUD-TX-003); any future nested acquire freezes every buy and exit of the wallet with no error (AUD-TX-001).

options.name: Priority lane for emergency exits plus holder tracking that throws on a nested acquire
options.behavior_impact: Anti-rug (and operator emergency) sells are served before queued routine ops and the running escalation yields at its next attempt boundary; a nested acquire fails loudly instead of hanging.
options.risk: The yielding escalation must re-read the nonce and reconcile its last attempt before continuing (an emergency sell consumes a nonce in between); more code on the most sensitive path.

options.name: Abortable buy escalation (stop between attempts when an emergency exit is waiting) plus throw on nested acquire
options.behavior_impact: A snipe stops escalating as soon as an exit needs the wallet; the exit then takes the lock.
options.risk: The aborted snipe can still land from its last sent bundle, so it must be reconciled before the exit signs; snipes are given up more often.

options.name: Take the lock per attempt instead of per escalation (other ops interleave between attempts)
options.behavior_impact: No op holds the wallet for more than one attempt plus its confirm window.
options.risk: Every attempt boundary becomes a nonce-advanced reconcile point; a still-pending earlier attempt can collide with an interleaved op, which the current design avoids by holding the lock.

options.name: Make the lock re-entrant for the holding async context (re-entrancy part only)
options.behavior_impact: A nested acquire by the holder runs immediately instead of deadlocking.
options.risk: Hides design errors and lets a nested op sign while the outer op still assumes it owns the nonce; does nothing for head-of-line blocking.

recommendation: Research recommendation (research SUMMARY OD-17): priority-lane-and-throw, i.e. enforce lock ownership with AsyncLocalStorage (throw on nested acquire) and give anti-rug exits a priority lane; bound the total hold of one escalation, and cancel or reconcile an exit that its caller abandoned.
default: Keep current behaviour until the owning phase decides (milestone contract). This card covers S1 capital findings, which cannot rest on the default: until it is decided and fixed it blocks the live re-entry gate.
behavior_impact: Decides how long a buy can make an emergency exit wait, and whether a nested lock call fails loudly or hangs forever.
needed_by: Phase 24 discussion before Wave A (capital fixes, after the Phase 23 real-path proof)
